figures: 1. Figure 1: Aggregate performance across all 50 model-prompt conditions.

2. Figure 2: Evaluation metrics heatmaps by model and strategy. Four panels show Strict Accuracy, Lenient Accuracy, Error Rate (labels 4/5), and Ambiguity Rate (label 3). Rows are models; columns are the five prompting strategies (no-role, public-health expert, respiratory specialist, public-health+time/id, respiratory+time/id). Brighter cells in the strict/lenient panels and darker cells in the error panel indicate stronger flagging.

3. Figure 3: Comprehensive evaluation metrics across strategies (box plots). For each strategy, box plots summarize cross-model distributions of Strict, Lenient, Error, Ambiguity, and Composite Score. Medians and IQRs show that expert-only prompts (no time/id) tend to yield higher strict/lenient and lower error, while adding time/id nudges models toward acceptance (higher error, similar or slightly lower ambiguity). The composite-score panel includes a zero reference for interpretability.
4. Figure 4: Quarterly trends in strict accuracy by model and strategy (strategy_quarterly_trends).

5. Figure A1: Model ranking by average composite score across strategies. Bars rank models by the mean composite score (higher is better; ambiguous = 0, correct rejections weighted more than mild judgments). The zero line indicates break-even (correct vs. incorrect judgments balanced).
6. Figure A2: Composite comparison figure showing heatmap, box plot, bar chart, and pie chart of results.
results_section: 1. Averaged across all models and prompts, the strict accuracy reached 48.0% and lenient accuracy was 61.2%.
2. The ambiguity rate was consistently low, under 2% overall.
3. Expert-only prompts (S2, S3) yield higher medians for lenient accuracy (around 65-70%) compared to context-augmented ones (S4, S5; around 55-60%).
4. error rates rising by 5-10 percentage points when context is added, particularly for models like Gemini (-13.8 pp in strict accuracy).
5. lenient accuracy differences are mostly negative (e.g., GPT-4o -10.0 pp, Gemini -8.1 pp)
6. with small positives for Llama-4 (+1.1 pp) and Mistral-Large (+0.9 pp)
7. Performance shows an early peak in 2022 Q2 (≈ 75–82%), followed by a sharp decline in Q3 and stabilization around 40–55% through 2023 Q1–Q3, with a modest rebound in Q4 (≈ 50–70%).
9. the lowest rates for DeepSeek-V3 and Gemini-2.5-Pro (≤1% across multiple regimes)
10. Error rates (false acceptances, labels 4/5) are higher for conservative models like GPT-4o, Llama-4 Maverick, and Mistral-Large (≈50%)
11. assertive models such as Doubao-Seed, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GLM-4 AirX, and Qwen3-235B-Thinking exhibit lower error rates (14-32%)
